questions.q: How do the authors define a strength?
a: Something you can do well repeatedly and enjoy
A skill you learned through hard practice
A talent you inherited from your parents
The thing your employer values most
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines a strength as an activity you can do repeatedly to perfection and enjoy.

questions.q: What did Gallup's survey of 198,000 workers find?
a: Using strengths daily linked to less turnover and better results
Most workers used their strengths every day
Weakness training raised customer satisfaction
Turnover was unrelated to how work felt
questions.why: Lesson 1 says employees who used strengths daily were more likely to be in lower-turnover, more productive firms.

questions.q: What is a talent, per the summary?
a: A thought or behavior pattern that makes things easier
A skill built only through repetition
A habit learned in childhood
A subject you studied at school
questions.why: Lesson 2 defines talent as a thought or behavior pattern that makes something easier than it is for most people.

a: By refining a talent with skills and knowledge
By correcting your worst weakness
By copying what successful people do
By waiting for the right opportunity
questions.why: Lesson 2 says developing a strength means refining natural talent with skills and knowledge.

questions.q: How can you spot your own talents?
a: Watch your instinctive reactions and what you learn fast
Ask friends to list your flaws
Take a test of general intelligence
Review your annual work targets
questions.why: Lesson 3 suggests watching everyday reactions, childhood interests and things you pick up quickly.
